newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian target of mid-1998 for open gas market.
newsitem.headline: Australian target of mid-1998 for open gas market.

text.p: The Australian gas reform Implementation Group (GRIG) said on Wednesday it hoped to have a long-delayed national access code in place nationally by June 1998.
"It may seem a long time, but the process is highly complex due to the nine jurisdictions involved," GRIG chairman Jon Stanford told a conference on gas reform.

Standford said GRIG expected the lead legislation for the code, which aims to provide open access to Australia's gas industry, would be introduced into the South Australian state parliament by October or November of this year.
He said this would be followed by applications for legislation of the code in other jurisdictions.
The draft code, finalised on June 30, would be released for public comment on July 4.
The gas reform implementation group comprises all state and territory governments, the gas industry and gas users.
Standford said a key sticking point in the code was how to implement an appeals process.
The code seeks to set up a regulatory framework which allows gas to be traded freely and fairly via Australia's gas pipelines, most of which are owned by private-sector operators.

The code was to have been finalised by mid-1996, but gas producers, distributers and users, as well as state and national governments, have failed to reach complete agreement, stalling progress toward the goal of a national spot market in gas.
The original draft code, released in September, was rejected by the Australian Gas Association (AGA) as heavy handed and sent back to the drawing board.
The AGA, which represents gas producers and the big ulitities which own gas piplines, said the original code handed too much power over access arrangements to regulators.
